what: Which entity routes carry an illustration, and therefore -- under the owner's ruling of 19 August 2026 -- which earn a whole two-page spread in the codex rather than an entry in a register spread. He ruled that a spread is EARNED by having an illustration; his words are in DECISIONS.md, where nothing tries to verify them against the corpus.
reading: This file is a BINDING and nothing else: entity id -> the plate file(s) that illustrate it. IT DOES NOT CARRY PROVENANCE. Hand, licence and subject live in arda_assets.json, which owns them, and are read from there. The first version of this file COPIED them in -- 370 KB, and a second place for a fact to go stale. A dataset every codex route fetches must carry only what those routes need.
expected_to_change: He also ruled that empty space is FILLED with art that fits, so this register GROWS. Every plate found promotes a route from a register entry to a spread of its own. Nothing should cache its contents.

measured.how: python3 map/spread_rule.py, and per family with spread_rule.earns_spread over git ls-files person/*.html place/*.html realm/*.html in site/. Never a grep of page HTML: the binding is by entity id in this register and the pages carry no , which is the false zero spread_rule.py records against itself.
measured.person: 429 of 431 -- the two without a bust are aglahad and mahtan, whose prompts exist and whose renders were never produced
measured.realm: 42 of 60 (19 Aug 2026). 31 were bound before this pass and 11 were added: alqualonde balar eregion fangorn khazaddum ladros lindon morgul shire tirion valinor. 18 remain dark and every one is dark because the archive holds no picture of its folk, its device or its ground -- angmar bombadil bree cardolan dolguldur dorthonion dorwinion druadan eotheod esgaroth himring lossoth nargothrond ossiriand reunited rhudaur thargelion utumno.
measured.place: 39 of 91 (19 Aug 2026). 13 were lit before this pass -- and only 4 of those 13 were bound AS places; the other 9 are realm rows read by a place route because both families share this register's `of` key. 26 were added. 52 remain dark, and this is still the archive's largest illustration gap: it holds SIX architectural views of a place in total (art/pl_*.jpg).
measured.note_on_collision: `of` IS THE KEY AND IT IS SHARED ACROSS FAMILIES, so a row recorded fam=realm lights a place route of the same id and vice versa. Ten routes are lit that way today -- angband belegost brethil dale erebor fangorn gondolin isengard nogrod rivendell. That is ruling 2a working as written (an id is unique within its COLLECTION, and `plates` is one collection), but it means `fam` records WHICH FAMILY THE BINDING WAS MADE FOR and never which routes it lights. Anyone counting per family must count routes, not rows.

unrecorded: CORRECTED 19 Aug 2026, and the earlier note here was wrong in the direction that manufactures work. It read that heraldry/gondor.svg, heraldry/redeye.svg and heraldry/rohan.svg are published with no row in arda_assets.json so the archive cannot state whose they are. TRUE HALF: no heraldry file has a row in arda_assets.json -- all 38 published ones, not three. FALSE HALF: the archive states whose they are perfectly well, in site/arda_heraldry_assets.json, which carries author, licence, source, basis and sha1 for 121 devices; map/licence_check.py READS that second register and says in its own source why copying the rows across would be the WRONG fix -- two registers holding the same rows must be kept in step by hand, which is the homograph fault this archive retires keys for. So licence_check being green over them is correct and is not the silence the old note took it for. What remains true is its arithmetic: licence_check reports 815 published / 775 recorded / 1 unrecorded, and 815 minus 775 is forty; the difference and the debt are two different populations and nobody has established why. Filed, not fixed.
why_person: a bust drawn to this archive's own portrait prompt, named by the entity id
why_realm: A realm in this archive is a PEOPLE as much as a ground, which is why a plate of a realm's own soldier illustrates it. Every realm binding here is DERIVED rather than remembered: the plate's own prompt in arda_soldier_prompts / arda_bestiary_prompts / arda_herbarium_prompts / arda_artifact_prompts names the realm, or arda_realms' own `race`, `aka` or `phases` field names the folk, tree or device the plate depicts. Where neither dataset makes the join, nothing is bound -- a plate chosen because it felt apt is a claim about what a thing LOOKED like, made without evidence.
why_place: A place binding is made only where THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN gazetteer note, or the plate's own prompt, names the thing depicted as belonging to that place -- Shelob's tunnel and the Stairs of Cirith Ungol, Sauron's werewolf-keep at Tol Sirion, the chief palantir stood under its Dome of Stars at Osgiliath. A creature, plant, artefact or soldier bound this way is NOT a view of the place and must be captioned with its own subject from arda_assets, never as a picture of the route. THE ARCHIVE STILL HOLDS ONLY SIX ARCHITECTURAL VIEWS of any place -- art/pl_*.jpg -- and that is the real gap; it is closed by rendering arda_place_prompts, whose population is ten hand-typed rows against 168 MAN_MADE places (map/gen_place_prompts.py --candidates), and not by binding harder.
